Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

improve verb

make better

also make better, improve on

classical

Sen. Ep. 6.1: nōn ēmendārī mē tantum sed trānsfigūrārī
Cic. Leg. 3.30 (Lewis & Short): tōta cīvitās ēmendārī et corrigī solet continentiā prīncipum
Traupman 154
Traupman 332

ēmendō, ēmendāre, ēmendāvī, ēmendātum

verb, first conjugation, transitive

improve, correct, free from faults

Lewis & Short: “to free from faults, to correct, improve, amend”: a text, a habit, one’s own life. Traupman gives it for “improve” with an object. The verb meliōrāre is post-classical (Dig.).

Other words

  • corrigō, corrigere, corrēxī, corrēctum — set right, correct

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Publ. P 62: Peccātum extenuat, quī celeriter corrigit.

    Of putting right what is wrong; Lewis & Short: “to improve, amend, correct, make better, reform”.

  • excolō, excolere, excoluī, excultum — refine, cultivate (the mind, manners, a place)

    verb, third conjugation, transitive · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 4.10.15: prōtinus excolimur tenerī; Cic. Arch. 12 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 303

    Lewis & Short: “to improve, ennoble, refine, perfect (the class. signif. of the word)”, as of minds trained by study.

  • meliōrem facere — make better

    also used · classical · Gell. 1.17.4 (Varro): quī fert, sēsē meliōrem facit

    The plain phrase for making a person or a thing better.

  • in melius mūtāre — change for the better

    also used · classical · M-O s.v. improve

    Morgan–Owens’s rendering; for the passive, Seneca’s in melius mūtārī, see improve, get better.

Examples

  • Intellegō, Lūcīlī, nōn ēmendārī mē tantum sed trānsfigūrārī.

    I can see, Lucilius, that I am not just being improved but transformed.Sen. Ep. 6.1

  • Ex vitiō alius sapiēns ēmendat suum.

    From another’s fault the wise man corrects his own.Publ. E 4

  • vitium … uxōris aut tollendum aut ferendum est. quī tollit vitium, uxōrem commodiōrem praestat, quī fert, sēsē meliōrem facit

    A wife’s fault must be either cured or borne: whoever cures it makes his wife easier to live with; whoever bears it makes himself better.Gell. 1.17.4 (Varro)

See also improve, develop, repair.
